chunks: From him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi, who said:

I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and with us was Abu Basir and some people from the Ahl al-Jabal, asking him about the sacrifices of the People of the Book. He said to them, 'You have heard what Allah said in His Book.'
They said to him, 'We would like you to inform us.' He said, 'Do not eat them.'
When we left his presence, Abu Basir said, 'Eat them, there is no harm in them,' for I had heard him and I had heard his father both commanding the eating of them.
So we returned to him, and Abu Basir said to me, 'Ask him.' I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, what do you say about the sacrifices of the People of the Book?'
He said, 'Did we not testify (give the ruling) this morning, and did you not hear?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Do not eat them.'
Abu Basir said to me, 'Eat them, there is no harm in them,' then said to me, 'Ask him a second time.'
He said to me the same as his first statement, and Abu Basir returned and said to me his first statement, 'Eat them, there is no harm in them.'
Then he said to me, 'Ask him,' so I said, 'I will not ask him after two times.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْجَبَلِ: The people of the mountain (a specific tribal group)
key_terms.ذَبَائِحِ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ: Sacrifices of the People of the Book
key_terms.فِي عُنُقِي: There is no harm in it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating the sacrifices of the People of the Book according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates the principle of *al-taqiyya* (dissimulation) through the contrasting behaviors of Abu Basir and the narrator; while Abu Basir concealed his true belief in permissibility to avoid contradicting the Imam publicly, the narrator adopted a more literal approach. It highlights the scholarly distinction between the general Quranic permission in Surah Al-Ma'idah and the specific contextual rulings or precautionary measures (*ihtiyat*) emphasized by the Imams regarding the sacrifices of the People of the Book.
